source_metadata.title: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Biologic Therapies for Moderate-to-Severe Crohn’s Disease: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis
source_metadata.source_type: systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials

extraction_metadata.scope_note: The primary evidence object is a systematic review/network meta-analysis. Pooled/network findings are review-level results. Trial-level endoscopic values from the supplement are retained as secondary reported evidence and are not presented as if the review enrolled those participants.

batch_manifest.semantic_scope: review objective, eligibility, search, endpoints, analysis, study selection and funding
biologic-naïve induction efficacy, direct and network estimates, rankings and supplement translation
biologic-experienced induction efficacy, prior-treatment heterogeneity and rankings
maintenance efficacy, serious adverse events, infections and endoscopic supplement
authors’ conclusions, strengths, limitations, funding and conflicts

atoms.canonical_statement: The review compared the relative efficacy and safety of TNF antagonists, vedolizumab, ustekinumab, and risankizumab, alone or with immunosuppressants, for moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease in biologic-naïve and biologic-exposed populations.
The investigators conducted a systematic review with pairwise and network meta-analysis; the review was not registered.

MEDLINE, EMBASE, and CENTRAL were searched from inception through June 3, 2021 without language restrictions; major gastroenterology conference proceedings from 2016–2021 were hand-searched and experts were contacted for unpublished data.
Eligible phase II or III RCTs enrolled adults aged at least 18 years with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease defined by CDAI 220–450.

population.label: Eligible adult RCT population

atoms.canonical_statement: Eligible trials evaluated infliximab, adalimumab, certolizumab pegol, vedolizumab, ustekinumab, or risankizumab, alone or with immunosuppressants, against placebo or another biologic, with at least 14 days of induction or 22 weeks of maintenance treatment.

population.label: Eligible treatment trials

atoms.canonical_statement: Pediatric trials, induction trials without results stratified by biologic-exposure status, and trials of advanced therapies without phase III data or not commonly used for moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease were excluded.

Two investigators independently screened records and full texts, and two investigators independently extracted study, participant, disease, and treatment data with discrepancies resolved by consensus or a third reviewer.
The primary induction efficacy outcome was clinical remission, defined as CDAI <150.
The secondary induction efficacy outcome was clinical response, defined as a CDAI reduction of at least 100 points from baseline.

outcome.definition: Reduction in CDAI by at least 100 points from baseline

atoms.canonical_statement: The primary maintenance efficacy outcome was maintenance of clinical remission (CDAI <150); serious adverse events and infections, using original study definitions, were the maintenance safety outcomes.
Efficacy analyses used intention-to-treat denominators with dropouts or missing data treated as nonresponders; last observation carried forward was used for safety endpoints.

Pairwise pooled odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals used DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models; heterogeneity was assessed with I² and funnel plots were used to examine small-study effects/reporting bias.
The network meta-analysis used frequentist multivariate consistency-model random-effects meta-regression in Stata 15, with relative treatment rankings summarized by SUCRA.
GRADE was used to rate confidence in direct and indirect efficacy estimates, considering risk of bias, indirectness, imprecision, inconsistency/heterogeneity, publication bias, and intransitivity.
The systematic review and network meta-analysis was unfunded, and the authors reported that no sponsor had a role in design, data collection, analysis, interpretation, or writing.
The search yielded 18,382 citations; after 7,584 duplicates were removed, 10,798 records were screened, 569 full texts reviewed, and 31 trials were eligible for inclusion.

population.label: Eligible randomized controlled trials

atoms.canonical_statement: Most included trials were judged at low risk of bias or uncertain risk of bias when only published in abstract form; funnel plots did not show evidence of small-study effects.
Only one active-comparator head-to-head biologic trial (ustekinumab versus adalimumab, SEAVUE) and two active-comparator combination-therapy trials were available to anchor direct comparisons.
Fifteen induction RCTs included 2,931 biologic-naïve patients with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease.

population.label: Biologic-naïve induction RCT population

atoms.canonical_statement: Direct meta-analysis found infliximab increased the odds of induction clinical remission versus placebo (OR 6.55, 95% CI 2.31–18.55).

population.label: Biologic-naïve adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease (CDAI 220–450)

atoms.canonical_statement: Direct meta-analysis found adalimumab increased the odds of induction clinical remission versus placebo (OR 5.31, 95% CI 2.99–9.43).

population.label: Biologic-naïve adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease (CDAI 220–450)

atoms.canonical_statement: In the SEAVUE head-to-head trial, ustekinumab did not improve induction clinical remission versus adalimumab (OR 1.11, 95% CI 0.74–1.65).

population.label: Biologic-naïve adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease (CDAI 220–450)

atoms.canonical_statement: Adding azathioprine to adalimumab did not improve induction clinical remission versus adalimumab alone (OR 0.57, 95% CI 0.29–1.10).

population.label: Biologic-naïve adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease (CDAI 220–450)

atoms.canonical_statement: Infliximab plus azathioprine was superior to infliximab monotherapy for induction clinical remission in a direct comparison (OR 1.65, 95% CI 1.07–2.54).

population.label: Biologic-naïve adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease (CDAI 220–450)

atoms.canonical_statement: Network meta-analysis supported Infliximab over certolizumab pegol for induction of clinical remission in biologic-naïve patients (OR 4.53, 95% CI 1.49–13.79); the review rated these estimates at moderate confidence.

population.label: Biologic-naïve adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease (CDAI 220–450)

atoms.canonical_statement: Network meta-analysis supported Infliximab + azathioprine over certolizumab pegol for induction of clinical remission in biologic-naïve patients (OR 7.49, 95% CI 2.04–27.49); the review rated these estimates at moderate confidence.

population.label: Biologic-naïve adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease (CDAI 220–450)

atoms.canonical_statement: Network meta-analysis supported Adalimumab over certolizumab pegol for induction of clinical remission in biologic-naïve patients (OR 3.01, 95% CI 1.25–7.27); the review rated these estimates at moderate confidence.

population.label: Biologic-naïve adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease (CDAI 220–450)

atoms.canonical_statement: Network meta-analysis supported Ustekinumab over certolizumab pegol for induction of clinical remission in biologic-naïve patients (OR 2.63, 95% CI 1.10–6.28); the review rated these estimates at moderate confidence.

population.label: Biologic-naïve adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease (CDAI 220–450)

atoms.canonical_statement: Network meta-analysis favored infliximab plus azathioprine over vedolizumab for induction clinical remission (OR 3.76, 95% CI 1.01–14.03), but confidence was low because of indirectness.

population.label: Biologic-naïve adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease (CDAI 220–450)

atoms.canonical_statement: For biologic-naïve induction remission, SUCRA rankings were infliximab plus azathioprine 0.96, infliximab 0.81, adalimumab 0.67, ustekinumab 0.58, risankizumab 0.49, vedolizumab 0.45, and certolizumab pegol 0.15.

In the GALAXI sensitivity analysis, guselkumab was highly ranked (SUCRA 0.79), based on 45 of 73 patients (61.6%) achieving induction clinical remission; rankings of other agents were otherwise unchanged.

population.label: Biologic-naïve adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease (CDAI 220–450)

atoms.canonical_statement: The review reported no significant heterogeneity for biologic-naïve induction-remission estimates and no inconsistency on loop-specific analysis where direct and indirect evidence were both available.

Supplemental Table 6 translated the network estimates into anticipated biologic-naïve remission proportions assuming a 20% placebo remission rate: 71.8% infliximab plus thiopurine, 60.7% infliximab, 50.6% adalimumab, 47.2% ustekinumab, 42.7% risankizumab, 40.4% vedolizumab, 36.8% adalimumab plus thiopurine, and 25.4% certolizumab pegol.
Ten induction RCTs included 2,479 patients with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease and previous biologic exposure.

population.label: Biologic-experienced induction RCT population

atoms.canonical_statement: The biologic-experienced trials differed materially in prior-treatment history: MOTIVATE allowed failure of up to five biologics, whereas GAIN excluded primary infliximab nonresponders and enrolled patients with prior infliximab response or intolerance.

population.label: Adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease (CDAI 220–450) with previous biologic exposure

atoms.canonical_statement: Direct meta-analysis found Ustekinumab increased the odds of induction clinical remission versus placebo in biologic-experienced patients (OR 2.55, 95% CI 1.39–4.69).

population.label: Adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease (CDAI 220–450) with previous biologic exposure

atoms.canonical_statement: Direct meta-analysis found Risankizumab increased the odds of induction clinical remission versus placebo in biologic-experienced patients (OR 2.64, 95% CI 1.89–3.68).

population.label: Adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease (CDAI 220–450) with previous biologic exposure

atoms.canonical_statement: Direct meta-analysis found Adalimumab increased the odds of induction clinical remission versus placebo in biologic-experienced patients (OR 3.55, 95% CI 1.82–6.93).

population.label: Adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease (CDAI 220–450) with previous biologic exposure

atoms.canonical_statement: Vedolizumab did not significantly improve induction clinical remission versus placebo in biologic-experienced patients (OR 1.25, 95% CI 0.63–2.49), although clinical response was improved (OR 1.77, 95% CI 1.06–2.94).

population.label: Adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease (CDAI 220–450) with previous biologic exposure

atoms.canonical_statement: Network meta-analysis favored risankizumab over vedolizumab for induction clinical remission in biologic-experienced patients (OR 2.10, 95% CI 1.12–3.92), with moderate confidence.

population.label: Adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease (CDAI 220–450) with previous biologic exposure

atoms.canonical_statement: Network meta-analysis favored adalimumab over vedolizumab for induction clinical remission after prior biologic exposure (OR 2.82, 95% CI 1.20–6.62), but confidence was low because of imprecision and indirectness related to selective GAIN eligibility.

population.label: Adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease (CDAI 220–450) with previous biologic exposure

atoms.canonical_statement: For induction remission in biologic-experienced patients, SUCRA rankings were adalimumab 0.92, risankizumab 0.77, ustekinumab 0.53, and vedolizumab 0.23; the adalimumab ranking was driven by selective GAIN enrollment.

Supplemental Table 6 estimated remission proportions assuming a 10% placebo remission rate in biologic-exposed patients: 28.3% adalimumab, 22.7% risankizumab, 18.0% ustekinumab, and 12.3% vedolizumab.
No direct head-to-head active-comparator trials were available in biologic-experienced patients; comparative estimates in this network were therefore indirect.
Fifteen maintenance RCTs included 3,786 patients; most used responder re-randomization designs, while three were treat-through trials.

population.label: Maintenance RCT population

atoms.canonical_statement: All evaluated biologic therapies were superior to placebo for maintenance of remission, but the network meta-analysis found no individual agent clearly superior to another; evidence for active-versus-placebo maintenance efficacy was rated moderate.
Maintenance SUCRA rankings were highest for infliximab plus azathioprine (0.87), adalimumab (0.78), and infliximab monotherapy (0.63); excluding treat-through trials produced similar rankings.

For serious adverse events, infliximab plus azathioprine was associated with lower risk than infliximab monotherapy (OR 0.56, 95% CI 0.33–0.97); serious adverse events included worsening Crohn’s disease under original trial definitions.

population.label: Adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease in maintenance randomized controlled trials

outcome.definition: As defined by original trial authors; definitions included worsening Crohn’s disease

atoms.canonical_statement: Adalimumab was associated with more infections than placebo during maintenance therapy (OR 1.54, 95% CI 1.17–2.01).

population.label: Adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease in maintenance randomized controlled trials

outcome.definition: As defined by original maintenance trial authors

atoms.canonical_statement: Infliximab was associated with fewer infections than adalimumab in the maintenance safety network (OR 0.54, 95% CI 0.33–0.90).

population.label: Adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease in maintenance randomized controlled trials

outcome.definition: As defined by original maintenance trial authors

atoms.canonical_statement: Infliximab + azathioprine was associated with fewer infections than adalimumab in the maintenance safety network (OR 0.46, 95% CI 0.24–0.89).

population.label: Adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease in maintenance randomized controlled trials

outcome.definition: As defined by original maintenance trial authors

atoms.canonical_statement: Ustekinumab was associated with fewer infections than adalimumab in the maintenance safety network (OR 0.69, 95% CI 0.50–0.97).

population.label: Adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease in maintenance randomized controlled trials

outcome.definition: As defined by original maintenance trial authors

atoms.canonical_statement: Infection SUCRA rankings, where higher values indicated lower infection risk, were infliximab plus azathioprine 0.90, infliximab 0.77, ustekinumab 0.55, vedolizumab 0.41, adalimumab 0.16, and certolizumab pegol 0.10.

Short induction trials were not used for safety analysis, and maintenance RCTs were underpowered for rare safety events; safety rankings were also distorted by SAE definitions that included worsening Crohn’s disease.

Supplemental Table 3 showed heterogeneous endoscopic endpoint definitions; examples included week-26 mucosal healing of 43.9% with infliximab plus azathioprine versus 30.1% with infliximab alone in SONIC, and week-12 endoscopic response of 40.3% with risankizumab versus 12.0% placebo in ADVANCE.

The authors concluded that infliximab and adalimumab, as monotherapy or with azathioprine, remain important first-line options for inducing and maintaining remission in moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease.

For patients with previous TNF-antagonist exposure, the authors identified IL23-pathway blockade with ustekinumab or risankizumab as a potentially more effective strategy, while emphasizing that treatment choices should be individualized.
The authors stated that network estimates should supplement, rather than replace, physician experience, cost/resource constraints, and patient values and preferences when selecting therapy.
The evidence base contained few direct head-to-head biologic trials, so many active-treatment comparisons depended on indirect network evidence.

Clinical remission (CDAI <150) was the primary efficacy outcome; heterogeneity in corticosteroid-free and endoscopic endpoint definitions prevented pooled network analysis of those increasingly important outcomes.

Trials spanned roughly two decades and enrolled increasingly refractory populations with differences in disease duration, prior biologic failures, and assessment timing; the absence of individual-patient data limited control of effect modifiers and unmeasured confounders.
Maintenance evidence mixed responder re-randomization and treat-through designs, although sensitivity analyses excluding treat-through studies did not materially change rankings.
The review was not prospectively registered.

The authors highlighted three major updates over prior network meta-analyses: inclusion of the SEAVUE head-to-head trial, incorporation of infliximab/adalimumab combination-therapy trials, and inclusion of phase III risankizumab data.
The study received no industry funding; the article separately disclosed extensive author consulting, speaking, research, and advisory relationships with multiple pharmaceutical companies.
Several authors reported financial relationships with manufacturers of biologic or advanced therapies evaluated in the review; one author reported no relevant disclosures.
